title: Ansel and the Orbit
premise: Odile Marchetti, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo through contested orbits, is the only witness when gravity fails for nine seconds system-wide — a signature she recognizes from a weapon she once carried. The glitch is the first tremor of a dying orbital engine built by the Founders, whose cryosleeping descendants hold the codes to restart Earth's last transmission loop. Hunted by a salvage syndicate that wants the codes sold and by an old commander who wants them buried, Odile gathers a ragtag crew of debtors, defectors, and one runaway child who reminds her of the soldiers she failed. In the end, Odile chooses to wake the forgotten half of humanity — the conscripted, the criminal, the poor — and sacrifices her own memory core to stabilize the engine, waking to a family she can no longer remember but who refuse to let her face the new system alone.
about_author: Theo Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics draftsman who turned to fiction after a decade spent drawing ships that were never built. They write quiet, mechanical futures where machines grieve better than people do.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hauling scrap through the Verge, she experiences the nine-second gravity flicker and recognizes the harmonic as the signature of the Halcyon engine — the war machine she helped carry to its hiding place ten years ago. Beat: dread of a past that refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Lies
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A syndicate broker offers triple pay for a cargo run to the dead moon Cael, exactly where the engine sleeps. She refuses, then finds her debt ledger mysteriously tripled overnight. Beat: the trap closing; invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Passenger in Cryo Wrap
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Smuggled aboard as cargo: Pip, a twelve-year-old runaway from the cryo-colonies carrying half a Founder access key tattooed in subdermal ink. Odile intends to dump her at the next station. Beat: reluctant tenderness, the first crack in Odile's armor.

chapters.title: What the War Owes
chapters.summary: Commander Reyes's POV. Reyes, Odile's former handler, is ordered by the Founders' council to erase the engine and everyone who knows of it — including Odile. He requests the assignment personally, telling himself it's mercy. Beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Verge Convoy
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ambushed by syndicate raiders, Odile is saved by a convoy of debtor-haulers who consider her a legend of the labor wars. She accepts their escort and, grudgingly, their friendship. Beat: found family forming in the margins of the law.

chapters.title: Cael, Where the Engine Dreams
chapters.summary: Odile and Pip's alternating POV. Inside the derelict Founders' vault, they find the Halcyon engine failing and a cryo-bay split in two: one wing holding the elite, one holding the conscripts nobody counted. Pip's key fits the conscript wing. Beat: horror at the arithmetic of who gets saved.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes boards Odile's ship under a truce flag, offering her erasure of her debts in exchange for letting the conscript wing die quietly. Odile counters by showing him the manifest of the elite wing — his own family's names. Beat: the law's price made personal.

chapters.title: The Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Earth's final transmission loop begins its last cycle; once it ends, no one wakes. The syndicate fleet arrives to seize the engine, and the debtor convoy arrives to defend it. Reyes must choose a side in orbit above Cael. Beat: all threads converge; rising chaos.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds to Hold the Sky
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. The engine can be stabilized only by a compatible neural core — hers. Odile docks herself into the machine as gravity flickers again, buying the system nine seconds that become nine hours, while Pip and the convoy fight to hold the vault. Beat: sacrifice as the ultimate act of chosen family.

chapters.title: Waking to Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, then Odile's. The conscript wing wakes; the elite wing's fate is decided by a vote of the newly risen. Odile reboots with her war memories gone, a stranger in her own hull — and finds the convoy, Pip, and even Reyes waiting with her ledger burned to zero. Beat: memory lost, family kept; justice outside the law, finally at rest.
